records.student_action: Interpret the shared stimulus, carry evidence forward between connected parts, and justify a physics plan/model choice.
records.student_text:
The diagram shows a box moving to the right at constant speed while a push acts to the right and friction acts to the left. Use the same situation for all parts.
(a) Identify the two horizontal forces shown.
(b) What must the horizontal net force be if the box is moving at constant speed in a straight line?
(c) If the push is 35 N to the right, use your answer from part (b) to determine the friction force.
(d) A student says, “Because the box moves at constant speed, no forces are acting.” Use the diagram and your earlier answers to correct the statement.
records.student_html:
The diagram shows a box moving to the right at constant speed while a push acts to the right and friction acts to the left. Use the same situation for all parts.

(a) Identify the two horizontal forces shown.

(b) What must the horizontal net force be if the box is moving at constant speed in a straight line?

(c) If the push is 35 N to the right, use your answer from part (b) to determine the friction force.

(d) A student says, “Because the box moves at constant speed, no forces are acting.” Use the diagram and your earlier answers to correct the statement.
records.answer: (a) push and friction; (b) 0 N; (c) 35 N left; (d) forces act, but they balance so net force is zero.
records.answer_text: (a) push and friction; (b) 0 N; (c) 35 N left; (d) forces act, but they balance so net force is zero.
records.solution_text: Constant straight-line velocity means zero net force. The rightward push and leftward friction therefore have equal magnitudes. With 35 N right, friction is 35 N left. The correct idea is no net force, not no forces.
records.solution_html: Constant straight-line velocity means zero net force. The rightward push and leftward friction therefore have equal magnitudes. With 35 N right, friction is 35 N left. The correct idea is no net force, not no forces.

Use the book-on-table force diagram to identify the net-force condition. Which statement best describes the forces on the book?

  1. Weight acts down and support force acts up; they can balance.
  2. Only weight acts because the book is not moving.
  3. Only support force acts because the table holds the book.
  4. Inertia acts upward to cancel gravity.

choices.text: Weight acts down and support force acts up; they can balance.
Only weight acts because the book is not moving.
Only support force acts because the table holds the book.
Inertia acts upward to cancel gravity.

records.answer: Weight acts down and support force acts up; they can balance.
